[h1]Medal of Honor (2010) Review[/h1]

[b]Medal of Honor (2010)[/b] is one of those games that really stuck with me.

[h2]Gameplay & Experience[/h2]
Back when I was playing regularly, I was [b]really[/b] good at it—dropping 50+ kills in matches. To the point where I’d actually get [u]kicked for suspected cheating[/u], which says a lot about how intense and competitive the multiplayer could get.

The gunplay felt solid, and at the time, the pacing hit that perfect balance between tactical and fast-paced action.

[h2]Setting & Atmosphere[/h2]
What made this game stand out was its grounding in real-world events. Set during the war in Afghanistan, it brought a modern warfare feel that reflected what was actually happening at the time. Maps like Kandahar and other high-conflict areas added a layer of realism and intensity that you didn’t always see in shooters back then.

[h2]The Downsides[/h2]
The biggest issue I ran into was the lack of proper anti-cheat systems. Instead of real detection, players would just vote-kick—so if you were playing too well, you were out. That definitely took away from the experience.

Also, coming back to it now might feel a bit rough. [i]Movement mechanics in modern FPS games have evolved a lot[/i], so it may feel dated compared to what we’re used to today.

[hr][/hr]

[h3]Final Thoughts[/h3]
I’ve been thinking about reinstalling it just for the nostalgia. It was a great game for its time, with memorable multiplayer moments and a grounded, intense setting. Even if it’s probably not as active anymore, it’s one of those titles that’s worth revisiting—if only to relive those peak moments.
